title: Number of 1 Bits
description:
# Number of 1 Bits

Write a function that takes a 32-bit integer `n` and returns the number of `1` bits in its binary representation. This count is also called the Hamming weight.

In Java the parameter type is signed `int`, but this problem is about the underlying 32-bit pattern. Negative values must therefore be counted by their two's-complement representation.

Negative values also have exactly 32 bits. For example, `-1` has 32 one bits; `-3` has pattern `11111111111111111111111111111101`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** n = 11
**Output:** 3
**Explanation:** The 32-bit pattern for 11 ends with `1011`, which has three set bits.

## Example 2:

**Input:** n = 128
**Output:** 1
**Explanation:** 128 is a power of two, so exactly one bit is set.

## Example 3:

**Input:** n = -3
**Output:** 31
**Explanation:** Java represents -3 as `11111111111111111111111111111101`, which has thirty-one set bits.

## Constraints:

* `n` is treated as one 32-bit integer value.

solutions.name: Brian Kernighan Lowest-Bit Clearing
solutions.description:
## Approach
Repeatedly replace `n` with `n & (n - 1)`. This operation clears the lowest set bit of the current 32-bit pattern. Count how many times this can be done before the pattern becomes zero.

## Key Insight
The expression `n & (n - 1)` removes exactly one `1` bit and leaves all higher bits unchanged. The loop runs once per set bit, so sparse values finish faster than a fixed 32-step scan.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(k), where k is the number of set bits. Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: Unsigned Right-Shift Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach
Repeat exactly 32 times. At each step, add the current lowest bit with `n & 1`, then shift the value right with the unsigned shift operator `>>>`.

## Key Insight
Using `>>>` is essential in Java because it fills high bits with zero. A signed right shift would keep reintroducing `1` bits for negative values and can make the loop incorrect.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(32), which is O(1) for fixed-width integers. Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: Moving Mask Check
solutions.description:
## Approach
Keep the input unchanged and move a single-bit mask from the least significant bit to the most significant bit. If `(n & mask) != 0`, the current position contains a `1`.

## Key Insight
A moving mask avoids shifting the signed input at all. This makes the two's-complement interpretation explicit: every one of the 32 bit positions is inspected exactly once, including the sign bit.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(32), which is O(1). Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: Byte Lookup Table
solutions.description:
## Approach
Precompute the number of set bits for every byte value from 0 to 255. Split the 32-bit integer into four bytes with unsigned shifts and masks, then add the four table results.

## Key Insight
Many bit-counting tasks repeat the same small subproblem. A 256-entry table turns each byte into a direct lookup while still preserving fixed, constant memory for this problem.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(1). Space Complexity: O(1) because the lookup table has fixed size.

solutions.name: SWAR Parallel Bit Count
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use a sequence of masks and shifts to add bit counts in parallel: first within 2-bit groups, then 4-bit groups, then bytes, and finally across the whole 32-bit word.

## Key Insight
SWAR stands for SIMD Within A Register. Instead of looping over positions, it treats the integer as many small counters packed into one register and combines those counters with carefully chosen masks.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(1). Space Complexity: O(1).

tests.description: Decimal eleven has three set bits in its 32-bit representation.
Power of two has exactly one set bit.
Signed negative input is counted by its two-complement bit pattern.
One has exactly one set bit.
All bits set in negative one produce a count of thirty-two.
Low byte filled with ones has eight set bits.
Another power of two checks higher-bit positions.
Largest positive int has every bit set except the sign bit.
The minimum int has only the sign bit set.
Alternating 0101 bits contain sixteen set positions.
Alternating 1010 bits are negative as a signed int but still have sixteen set bits.
